sentences.text: In 2024, the influence index stands at 36.2 for China (band 28.9–76.5, from 4 of six components) and 5.7 for the United States (band 5.0–46.5, from 4 of six components). The net lean is +30.5 points toward China.
Over the five years to 2024, the index for China rose by 9.5 points and the index for the United States fell by 6.1 points.

The value for China rests on trade export share, trade import share, debt stock and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.

The value for the United States rests on trade export share, trade import share, finance flow and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.
In 2025, 28% of Bolivia's mineral exports (UN Comtrade value US$5.3 bn) went to China and 4.2% to the United States; together 32%, the rest to other destinations.
Since 2020 the share going to China rose by 20.1 points and the share going to the United States was broadly flat.
Relative to the twelve-country export basket, its exports are specialised in gallium germanium antimony (RCA 25.9), zinc (RCA 24.3) and tungsten (RCA 23.8).
5 sudden shifts in export shares are flagged from the customs data, the latest in 2017: Exports to China fell from 25% to 1% of tin exports between 2016 and 2017 (reported by BOL to UN Comtrade).
AidData records US$2.1 bn of documented commitments from Chinese institutions to Bolivia over 2001–2021 (56 events; the source ends in 2021).
The DFC and OPIC records show US$2 m of documented commitments from US institutions to Bolivia over 2011–2023 (7 events).
Public and publicly guaranteed external debt owed to China was 2.3% of GDP in 2024 (World Bank IDS); no comparable series exists for debt owed to the United States.

The lenders with the largest recorded commitments to named recipients here are Export-Import Bank of China (China Eximbank) (US$2.7 bn), China Development Bank (CDB) (US$559 m) and Unspecified Chinese Government Institution (US$74 m).
Flags: documented commitments reached at least 1% of GDP in a year in 2010, 2015 and 2016 (documented).
Flags: large commitments were not followed by any change in the mineral trade share with the lender in 2015 (strongly indicated).
In the UN General Assembly, voting agreement in 2024 was 89% with China and 27% with the United States.
Since 2019, agreement with China was broadly flat and agreement with the United States rose by 8.4 points.
Too few mineral-related legislative records naming either actor have been scored for a stance series (five per year are needed); the text model is zero-shot baseline, not yet validated.

After Executive Order 13817: A Federal Strategy to Ensure Secure and Reliable Supplies of Critical Minerals (2017-12), the share of exports to the United States moved -19.7 points (28% before, 8.0% after); placebo p 0.25 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on graphite items in force (Announcement 2023 No. 39 of 20 October 2023) (2023-12), the share of exports to China moved +17.8 points (8.4% before, 26% after); placebo p 0.08 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on gallium and germanium items in force (MOFCOM/GAC Announcement 2023 No. 23 of 3 July 2023) (2023-08), the share of exports to China moved +17.8 points (8.4% before, 26% after); placebo p 0.08 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

Relative to the countries outside its scope, Bolivia: the YLB–ACI Systems lithium joint venture decree is repealed (DS 4070, 2 November) and President Morales resigns (10 November) is followed by a -2.1 points difference-in-differences in the share of exports to the United States (permutation p 0.63).

Relative to the countries outside its scope, Bolivia: the YLB–ACI Systems lithium joint venture decree is repealed (DS 4070, 2 November) and President Morales resigns (10 November) is followed by a -6.4 points difference-in-differences in the share of exports to China (permutation p 0.28).

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to China in 2030 is 34% (90% band 25%–46%), from random walk with drift, which beat naive persistence by 4% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to the United States in 2030 is 2.9% (90% band 0.0%–36%), from naive persistence, because no model beat it in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.
The published forecast for the influence index of China in 2030 is 36.1 (90% band 27.4–44.3), from naive persistence, because no model beat it in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of the United States in 2030 is 15.6 (90% band 0.0–37.7), from damped local linear trend (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood), which beat naive persistence by 6% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.
Under the stated scenarios the 2030 median share to China ranges from 24% (US sourcing rules bite) to 44% (accelerated China pull); these are what-ifs with a fixed yearly shift, not predictions.

In 2025, unavailable components: legislative stance (no scored legislative records naming the actor); debt stock (no source for debt owed to the United States); finance flow (source coverage ends 2021); debt stock and diplomatic alignment (source coverage ends 2024).

Source coverage ends at different years: Chinese official finance to 2021, US finance to 2026, debt by creditor to 2024, UN votes to 2024 and trade to 2025; components beyond a source's coverage are unavailable, not zero.
13 of the dated events used above are still in the draft event list awaiting the project owner's review.
Stance values come from the text model (zero-shot baseline, not yet validated); the rest of this brief rests on official statistics and the registered databases, each cited on its chart.

human.title: Bolivia: warm words for Washington, silver and zinc for Beijing
human.author: AI-drafted from the site's indicators; not yet reviewed by the project owner
human.text_md:
## Alignment

Bolivia's index leans firmly toward China: 36.3 against 5.7 for the United States in 2024, on four components each, the lowest US value among the countries with an index [index_value:influence:CN:2024] [index_value:influence:US:2024]. The trade behind it is silver, zinc, gold and tin, worth US$5.3 bn in 2025, of which 28% went to China and 4.2% to the United States; China took US$922 m of the US$1.9 bn of silver [concentration:share_cn_x:2025] [flow_trade:BOL:silver:2025]. The executives' coded statements are nonetheless warmest toward the United States (+1.00 over four) and neutral toward China (0.00 over three), a hedging balance of 0.67 [statement:stance_us:BOL:2024-2026] [statement:stance_cn:BOL:2024-2026] [insights:hedging:BOL]. Lithium takes 61% of the mineral mentions in Bolivian statements and 0.4% of the export value; silver is 36% of the value and a tenth of the mentions [insights:talk_vs_trade_minerals:BOL]. My reading: the political conversation is about the lithium that is not yet sold, while the dependence that exists is in silver and zinc.

## Trajectory

The Chinese share of exports rose from 4% in 2008 to 15% in 2016, fell back to 8% in 2020 and reached 28% in 2025, the largest five-year rise of the Chinese index in the region after Brazil's (+9.6 points) [concentration:share_cn_x:2025] [index_value:influence:CN:2024]. Chinese commitments were US$1.7 bn over 2015–2021, concentrated in 2015–2017, and no US commitment is recorded in either window [flow_finance:CN:BOL:2015-2021] [flow_finance:US:BOL:2015-2021]. Five sudden trade shifts and three large commitments are flagged [anomaly_flag:sudden_trade_shift] [anomaly_flag:large_commitment]. The 2019 repeal of the YLB–ACI Systems decree and the resignation of President Morales sit in the event list; the windows around the 2022 US measures and the 2023 Chinese export controls show the share to China rising 12 to 18 points, with placebo values near 0.08 [event_effect:us_inflation_reduction_act:CN:window:BOL] [event_effect:cn_export_control_graphite:CN:window:BOL]. No legislative records or press headlines are coded for Bolivia, so the executives' statements are the only words the site holds [coverage:BOL].

## Risks and likely next moves

The models put China's share at 34% in 2030 at baseline, 44% under the China pull and 24% under US reshoring; the US share stays under 13% in every path [forecast:export_share:CN:baseline:2030:BOL] [forecast:export_share:US:us_reshoring:2030:BOL]. Parity would take US$628 m of yearly exports switching, 2.8 times current US purchases, and silver alone could cover it [insights:parity_gap:BOL]. My reading: the next move that matters is whether any lithium contract (with Chinese, Russian or other partners) produces exports at all; until it does, Bolivia's dependence on China is a silver-and-zinc story that no US policy addresses.

## What would change this reading

Reported lithium exports of any size; a US commitment in the DFC or EXIM record; structured legislative records from the Asamblea, which the pipeline cannot obtain today; or a second coder who read the executives' warmth toward the United States differently.
